chief_complaint: irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, and weight gain
hpi_details: A 25-year-old female presents with irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, and weight gain that have gradually worsened.
ideas: She thinks that severe stress from her job and poor eating habits over the past year have completely thrown her hormones out of balance.
concerns: She is worried that these irregular cycles mean she will not be able to get pregnant when she and her partner try for a family.
expectations: She hopes to get medication to clear up her painful skin breakouts and bring her monthly cycle back on schedule.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes oral contraceptives, metformin, and weight loss for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Thyroid dysfunction without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: rapid onset or severe/virilising symptoms (voice deepening, clitoromegaly, very rapid hair growth), signs of Cushing syndrome (purple striae, buffalo hump, easy bruising), or onset well outside typical reproductive-age presentation.
management_principles: Plan for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Oral contraceptives, Metformin, weight loss
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A hormonal disorder causing anovulation and androgen excess, presenting with irregular periods, hirsutism, acne, and weight gain.
red_flags: Rapid onset or severe/virilising symptoms (voice deepening, clitoromegaly, very rapid hair growth) — raises concern for an androgen-secreting tumour rather than PCOS
Signs of Cushing syndrome (purple striae, buffalo hump, easy bruising) — needs screening for Cushing's rather than assuming PCOS
Onset well outside typical reproductive-age presentation — warrants evaluation for congenital adrenal hyperplasia or another endocrinopathy

My cycles used to be every thirty to thirty-five days, but over the last year they've stretched out to every two to three months and are totally unpredictable.
When I finally bleed, the flow is moderate for three or four days, soaking about three pads a day with occasional small clots, but it doesn't overflow.
Each period typically lasts around four to five days once it starts; it never drags on past a week.
It has now been almost two and a half months since the start of my last period.
No, I have never had spotting between cycles or any bleeding after having sex.

exam.finding: Alert, well-nourished young woman with moderate facial acne and excess terminal hair on the chin, in no acute distress; BMI is 27.8 kg/m2.
Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are anicteric.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, smooth, and without palpable nodules or bruits.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-distended without purple striae or surgical scars.
Soft, non-tender throughout; no palpable pelvic mass, enlarged uterus, or hepatosplenomegaly.
External genitalia appear normal without clitoromegaly; speculum and bimanual exam deferred pending chaperone and formal consent.

Coarse dark hairs noted on the chin, upper lip, and lower midline abdomen; inflammatory papules across the lower cheeks and jawline; faint hyperpigmentation with velvety texture at the posterior neck fold.
